newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends slightly higher in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends slightly higher in slow trade.

text.p: Trading activity eased due to a Canadian holiday but CME lumber futures recovered to close slightly higher on support from expectations interest rates will remain low, trader said.
Lumber closed $1.40 to $0.10 per thousand board feet higher with July up most at $399.90 and September up $0.30 at $387.90 per tbf.

Futures slowly moved up from a lower start, buoyed by trade expectations that interest rates will remain low. The majority of expectations are that the Federal Reserve on Tuesday will leave interest rates alone and this was seen keeping housing statistics strong going into the summer, traders said.
However, the continued quiet cash lumber market trade curbed futures gains. Futures moved up to point were mills look to hedge product, they said.
"Mills look to sell futures above $400," one trader said.
